notes: Cascade members are split by error text: test_17, 18, 19 have the same 'setup quota failed with 1' error as test_21 but are labelled ambient because that string appears on other uploaders' changes, test_22 and 25 are 'unmatched', and the root test_16b is labelled patch-changes-test with class ambient. Grouping should follow session order (first failure in a session, then everything after it that fails on the same broken setup) rather than error string; a rule that marks every failure after a patch-changed test that rebuilds the filesystem as one unit would catch this. The real bug is in 16b's sparse reformat/cleanup, not in tests 20/21.

why: test_43 log: after a delayed write via fail_loc 0x250, 'cmp: EOF on /mnt/lustre2/.../f43 after byte 4096', the second mount sees a short file; the patch is a WIP 'true async write commits' on the OST (tgt_brw_write replies before obd_commitrw, commit message TODO: handling of failed commits), and read-after-write mismatches of this kind hit sanityn, sanity, replay-single, sanity-pfl, sanity-pcc on this change only (ps4, 7, 8), 3 of 70 sessions passing.

selinux-ssk sessions only: writes return EPERM ('dd: error writing ... Operation not permitted'), migrate rc 5 follows; a separate failure of the deferred commit under SSK/nodemap identity, sanity 64j grant mismatch may belong to the grant bug instead

NULL dereference in lustre_msg_set_transno from tgt_last_rcvd_update under tgt_brw_write_commit: the commit uses a reply that is already gone

'client not evicted by ost1' in all 10 recovery-small sessions; this test fails that way occasionally elsewhere (about 10 times on other changes in 6 months) but here every time, so the patch makes it deterministic

Also, the change was abandoned in 2024 and re-uploaded as ps8 in 2026 'fortestonly': WIP patches like this produce hundreds of units and should probably be weighted or excluded so they do not dominate the eval.

why: test_24a's log ends with 'sysctl kernel.panic_on_warn1' and 'cannot stat /proc/sys/kernel/panic_on_warn1' on every node (exit 255), so the test returns 1 after its body passed; the patch adds panic_on_warn handling to test-framework.sh and ps10 builds the sysctl command without '='. bugs.units: nearly all 449 units across 24 suites (every 'test_N returned N', the 'Restart of mdsN/ostN failed!' units, and follow-on errors such as sanity 160o/160p changelog, 401gb, 413k, 429, 600a/600b, 854, sanity-quota 40d, recovery-small 156, sanity-hsm 24d)
bugs.reason: one cascade: the malformed 'sysctl kernel.panic_on_warn<N>' (also 'panic_on_warn0' in opted-out suites) runs in set_default_debug on every node at each test and mount, returns 255, so tests fail after passing, restarts are reported failed, and cleanups are cut short, leaving state that breaks later tests (sampled sanity, sanity-pcc, sanity-hsm, sanity-quota, insanity, ost-pools, recovery-small, conf-sanity, replay-single)

separate kernel bug exposed by the cascade: the MDT was left running, test_41b's 'mount -o nomgs,force' gets 'Operation already in progress' and the node oopses with a NULL dereference in ls_device_find_or_init, in all 5 conf-sanity sessions

separate: with panic_on_warn=1 a pre-existing kernel WARNING panics the node (in this patchset sanity-lfsck panics on the WARNING in osd_index_it_key from lfsck); these are real existing warnings, the patch's intent, not the typo

notes: A test-framework typo yields 449 units in 24 suites that are one bug; a selector that flags test-framework.sh changes as 'run everything' would catch it with any test. Grouping by sig fails here: 'test_N returned N' gives no error, and the true cause appears only as the last lines of each test log; checking whether a session's failures share a trailing log line would merge them. Where panic_on_warn turns pre-existing kernel WARNINGs into crashes, the crash is the patch's doing but the bug is old code; the eval should probably count those as distinct bugs the patch exposes rather than as its own. recovery-small 156 'client not evicted by ostN' also fails occasionally on other changes and may be ambient here.
